summary: full art and audio: every enemy and the boss through the M4 pipeline, environment modules and set dressing, final SFX, the second weapon and M4's two carried looks; done when no placeholder assets remain
read_first: docs/milestones/M6-plan.md §0, §1 (only the decisions your brief names) and §2 'File ownership', 'Shared files', 'Tuning' and 'ASSETS.md'
note: Phase 1. Every package needs only step 0, which is on the base: the ARCHITECTURE.md section with one '### <title> (<KEY>)' per package, the ASSETS.md headings, the narrowed palette ranges (plan §2 'Palette slots'), the signals CombatEvents.section_entered, barrier_moving and weapon_landed with Barrier's two emit lines, LevelSection.ambience and MoveData.impact_sfx. Every sound comes from ElevenLabs (Game-boy, 2026-11-04, plan D19): there is no Sonniss bundle. Game-boy's pick and the Tripo licence are both answered (HANDOFF d2a0cba, 0d6a5c9). PROPS is the only phase 1 package that uses the pick: weapon A = bike_chain (assets/source/concepts/m6/weapon_a.jpg) and the moods mood_street_a.jpg and mood_roof_a.jpg (the roof C). ASSETS rows for Tripo models read 'Tripo API (paid credits): owned by the project, commercial use'. Shared files are edited by region only, appending and never reordering (plan §2 'Shared files'): room_kit.gd (CHAIN the warm-up; KIT add_box, add_visual_box, box_mesh, build_environment), toon_materials.gd (the Kind enum: KIT and PROPS append; warm_up: CHAIN; swatch_glossy: LOOKS; art_prop: PROPS; trim: KIT), test_room.gd (CHAIN the dummies; AUDIO the audition room), test_art_contract.gd (CHAIN BUDGETS, _id_of and the report tests; LOOKS the palette tests), test_look_post.gd (KIT the environment checks; CHAIN lines 578-580), tuning_data.gd (your own subgroup; Debug lines appended at the group's end), weapon.gd (PROPS: art_scene and the floor tint on the art only). A package that adds or changes a palette JSON regenerates the atlas on its branch (python3 -I tools/pipeline/gen_palette.py). The lead merges each package as it finishes and regenerates the default preset, the atlas and the placeholder ratchet, so conflicts there are expected and fine. tests/fixtures/m6/placeholder_ratchet.json exists only on LOOKS's branch in this phase: every other package writes the inventory drop it expects (per scene and category, plan §2 'Placeholder inventory') in its calls file, and the lead sets the ratchet at merge. Paid services in this phase: Tripo and Gemini for PROPS only (Tripo ceiling 270 credits; the M6 ledger stop is 900, the floor 700); ElevenLabs for AUDIO only (ceiling 6000 credits). captures_dir holds M5's final recordings (street, roofs, boss, seams): the 'before' for every look.

packages.section: §3 'AUDIO: Ingest, manifest, voices and the audition room'
read: tools/pipeline/tripo.py (header, the ledger and policy functions: the ledger pattern)
tools/gemini_image.py lines 1-45 (the .env loader and its worktree fallback)
packages.note: ElevenLabs is the only paid service you may call: tools/audio/eleven_sfx.py, ceiling 6000 credits for this package, policy stop 30000 for M6 (eleven_policy.json max_call 1200, so a 30 s bed fits one call; the account is Starter with 40,000 credits). Never print, log or write the key (ELEVEN_LABS_API_KEY or ELEVENLABS_API_KEY in .env; in a worktree read the main checkout's .env as tools/gemini_image.py does), never put it in a URL. Your first call is one 0.5 s job to measure the real cost; write the rate in M6-calls/AUDIO.md, then apply your brief's projection rule before the batch. Downloads are untrusted: each job's MP3s go into a new empty folder and reach ffmpeg as path arguments. You can't hear: choose by measured features and leave judgement to Game-boy's audition. Every sound comes from ElevenLabs (Game-boy, 2026-11-04; plan D19): there is no Sonniss bundle, so ingest.py needs no Sonniss or SONNISS_DIR support. SFX (phase 2) fills the hit stack and the world slots with your eleven_sfx.py and ingest.py after you merge, so make both general: any pool, a loop flag, 2D or 3D, and a jobs file per group.
